title: 不是美国施压：日本央行早就想加息，贝森特施压后日债长端会怎样？
speaker: Masahiko Hikulu

segments.en: How do you, I mean, how do you factor in some of the U.S. dynamics now? When Scott Besson has really pressured the B.O.J. to really hike, you better hike, right? Obviously, they're thinking about their treasury yield curve and the light, but how do you think those dynamics are going to play out?
segments.zh: 您如何考虑美国方面的动态？当斯科特·贝森特真的向日本央行施压要求加息时，你们最好加息。显然，他们在考虑自己的国债收益率曲线，但您认为这些动态会如何演变？

segments.en: I think it's more like, you know, it's not really U.S. pressure in Japan per se, but Japan has always, you know, if you look at B.O.J. what they are doing, they have always wanted to hike, right? The only thing that stand between B.O.J. and hiking is politics, right?
segments.zh: 我认为这并不完全是美国对日本的压力，但如果你看看日本央行的所作所为，他们一直想要加息。唯一阻碍日本央行加息的是政治因素。

segments.en: We know that Takaiji and her, you know, advisers, they are against that before, you know, reasonable reason, right? Because they want Japan to have lower rates, they want to spend more in Japan, to revive Japan and get Japan out completely from the three decades of lost decades, right? Which is reasonable.
segments.zh: 我们知道高市及其顾问此前反对加息，原因合理。因为他们希望日本保持低利率，增加支出，重振日本，让日本彻底走出失去的三十年。这是合理的。

segments.en: If you look at B.O.J. what they have been doing, they have been sailing in the market, that inflation and the line inflation is pretty okay, right? If you take out all the, you know, institutional factors, it's around two, three percent. Growth in Japan is very sanguine, right? Consumption is slightly lower in Japan because inflation is eating in your real wages.
segments.zh: 如果你看看日本央行的行动，他们一直在市场中航行，通胀和核心通胀还算可以。如果剔除所有制度性因素，大约在2%到3%。日本增长非常乐观。消费略低，因为通胀侵蚀了实际工资。

segments.en: But then if you look at Japan, right? They are exports and some in conductor AI related investments is going up, it's not as, you know, huge, like, you know, ballistics like Korea and Taiwan, but Japan is one of the benefit fisher, right? Not beneficial from the whole AI exports too.
segments.zh: 但如果你看看日本，出口和一些半导体、AI相关投资正在上升，虽然不像韩国和台湾那样巨大，但日本也是受益者之一，从整个AI出口中受益。

segments.en: So the growth thing, everything, directly wise, is very sanguine and that's why B.O.J. is actually pushing for retight. And now we have Scott Besson coming to the equation, right? Why did Scott Besson come in? Because he's afraid that, you know, excessive yen or disorder yen movement would threaten Japan to intervene more and when Japan has to intervene, they sell their strategies, right?
segments.zh: 所以增长方面，一切都很乐观，这就是日本央行推动紧缩的原因。现在斯科特·贝森特加入进来。他为什么来？因为他担心日元过度或无序波动会迫使日本更多干预，而当日本干预时，他们会抛售资产。

segments.en: And if Japan intervenes more in the yen, yen is excessively weak, people will sell JGB too, right? And if the long-end JGB's curve, you know, steepen a lot, that put steepening pressure globally too. So that's why Scott Besson came in and helped, you know, B.O.J. and thus the whole thing, from the House comment? Yeah, I'm the House. I mean, their objectives are certainly aligned, putting it that way.
segments.zh: 如果日本更多干预日元，日元过度疲软，人们也会抛售日本国债。如果长端日本国债曲线大幅陡峭化，也会给全球带来陡峭化压力。所以斯科特·贝森特介入帮助日本央行，整个事情，从众议院评论？是的。我的意思是，他们的目标肯定是一致的。
